title: NMOSD / MOGAD acute attack
keyNumbers: Severe attack, or poor response to steroids → PLEX within 5 days of onset
Plasma exchange (PLEX): 1–1.5 total plasma volumes per exchange, daily or every other day; median 5 exchanges over ~10 days (range 2–10); albumin replacement
IVIG: 0.4 g/kg/day ×5 days if PLEX not feasible
presentation: Severe or bilateral optic neuritis; longitudinally extensive myelitis
Area postrema syndrome: intractable hiccups, nausea, vomiting
MOGAD: optic disc edema, perineural enhancement, ADEM, conus lesions, cortical encephalitis with seizures
definitions: AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD (Wingerchuk 2015): ≥1 core clinical characteristic + positive AQP4-IgG (cell-based assay recommended) + exclusion of alternatives. Core: optic neuritis, acute myelitis, area postrema syndrome, acute brainstem syndrome, symptomatic narcolepsy/diencephalic syndrome with typical lesions, symptomatic cerebral syndrome with typical lesions
AQP4-negative/unknown NMOSD: ≥2 core characteristics with dissemination, ≥1 being optic neuritis, LETM, or area postrema syndrome, plus MRI requirements

MOGAD (Banwell 2023): (A) core demyelinating event + (B) positive serum MOG-IgG by cell-based assay (clear positive alone; low positive/no titer/CSF-only needs AQP4-negative + ≥1 supporting clinical/MRI feature) + (C) exclusion of better diagnosis incl. MS

immediateActions.action: Serum AQP4-IgG and MOG-IgG (live cell-based assay preferred); steroids, IVIG, and PLEX can lower detection

immediateActions.window: Severe attack or no response in 48–72 h
immediateActions.action: Poor or absent steroid response → PLEX, ideally within 5 days of attack onset; in severe attacks give PLEX first-line or alongside steroids
MRI brain, orbits, and whole spine with contrast
Avoid starting MS disease-modifying therapies — some worsen NMOSD

notes: Serum preferred over CSF; repeat ≥3 months later or at relapse if negative and suspicion high

workup.test: MRI brain, orbits, whole spine with contrast

notes: OCB usually absent in NMOSD/MOGAD; pleocytosis can be marked

workup.test: Infection, B12/copper, ANA/SSA, ACE as indicated

treatment.doseText: 1 g IV daily ×3–5 days, then oral taper (MOGAD relapses can occur during weaning)
notes: Taper length individualized (weeks for AQP4; often longer for MOGAD)
evidenceNote: Standard practice; no RCT for attack treatment

treatment.doseText: 1–1.5 total plasma volumes per exchange, daily or every other day; median 5 exchanges over ~10 days (range 2–10); albumin replacement
notes: Each day of delay cut the odds of complete remission by ~6.3% (ASFA, citing Bonnan 2018/Kleiter 2018)
Steroids ×5 days then PLEX restored baseline in 51% vs 16.6% with steroids alone (ASFA, citing Abboud 2016)
AAN 2011 (since retired): possibly effective for fulminant CNS demyelination (Level C)

treatment.doseText: 0.4 g/kg/day ×5 days if PLEX not feasible

treatment.agent: Already on a C5 inhibitor (eculizumab, ravulizumab): supplemental dose with PLEX or IVIG
treatment.doseText: Eculizumab: after each PLEX session, 300 mg if the most recent dose was 300 mg, or 600 mg if it was ≥600 mg, within 60 min. Ravulizumab: after each PLEX session, within 4 h — 40 to <60 kg: 1,200 mg (most recent dose 2,400 mg) or 1,500 mg (3,000 mg); 60 to <100 kg: 1,500 mg (2,700 mg) or 1,800 mg (3,300 mg); ≥100 kg: 1,500 mg (3,000 mg) or 1,800 mg (3,600 mg); after completing an IVIG cycle, 600 mg within 4 h

dose.label: Eculizumab after PLEX (most recent dose 300 mg)
frequency: Within 60 min after each PLEX session

dose.label: Eculizumab after PLEX (most recent dose ≥600 mg)
frequency: Within 60 min after each PLEX session

dose.label: Ravulizumab after PLEX (by weight and most recent dose — see doseText)
frequency: Within 4 h after each PLEX session

dose.label: Ravulizumab after an IVIG cycle
frequency: Within 4 h after completing the IVIG cycle

notes: Eculizumab with IVIG: the label's IVIG supplement table is gMG-only — no NMOSD statement

pitfalls: Don't wait for AQP4/MOG results to treat
Interferon-beta, natalizumab, and fingolimod can worsen NMOSD
Low-titer MOG-IgG has lower specificity — interpret with the clinical/MRI picture
Bilateral optic neuritis and myelitis have the poorest remission rates — escalate early

On a C5 inhibitor (eculizumab, ravulizumab): signs of meningococcal infection → evaluate immediately, even if vaccinated (boxed warning); consider interrupting the drug during treatment of serious meningococcal infection
Meningococcal Patient Safety Card (REMS) is carried after stopping eculizumab (3 months) or ravulizumab (8 months)
Inebilizumab (Uplizna) and satralizumab (Enspryng): labels give no PLEX/IVIG guidance
escalateWhen: Severe attack, or poor response to steroids → PLEX within 5 days of onset
Respiratory compromise from high cervical myelitis → ICU
Confirmed diagnosis → neuroimmunology for relapse prevention
institutionVaries: AQP4/MOG send-out lab (live vs fixed cell-based assay)
Whether PLEX is started concurrently with steroids for severe attacks
REMS: eculizumab and ravulizumab are dispensed only by REMS-certified healthcare settings and pharmacies — confirm before PLEX so the supplemental dose can be given
